commands.review_summary:
The PR adds a 30-second `timeoutMs` to Google Chat's shared API response helper and adds mocked Vitest coverage for timeout wiring and abort propagation.

PR surface: Source +5, Tests +75. Total +80 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: no. high-confidence live reproduction was established. Source inspection does show current main has no deadline on the shared outbound Google Chat guarded fetch call, while the PR proof is mocked plus a reproduction sketch.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Manual handling is needed because contributor real-behavior proof is missing and maintainers must decide whether to split media/control deadlines or accept one global cap.

target.title: fix(googlechat): add 30 s request timeout to withGoogleChatResponse
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

All outbound Google Chat API calls (`sendGoogleChatMessage`, `updateGoogleChatMessage`,
`deleteGoogleChatMessage`, `uploadGoogleChatAttachment`, `downloadGoogleChatMedia`,
`createGoogleChatReaction`, `listGoogleChatReactions`, `deleteGoogleChatReaction`,
`findGoogleChatDirectMessage`, `getGoogleChatSpace`, `probeGoogleChat`) flow through
`withGoogleChatResponse` in `extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts`. That helper calls
`fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a `timeoutMs` or `signal`, so if `chat.googleapis.com`
accepts the TCP connection but never completes the HTTP response (stalled server, network
middlebox, proxy delay), the call blocks indefinitely.

This pins a gateway request lane open with no ceiling. Under sustained inbound traffic,
multiple stalled reply calls accumulate and can exhaust the available concurrency,
preventing all other messages from being processed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` accepts a top-level `timeoutMs` parameter (line 80,
`src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts`) that is forwarded to the underlying request handler as
an abort deadline. Adding `timeoutMs: GOOGLECHAT_API_TIMEOUT_MS` to the single shared
`withGoogleChatResponse` helper covers every call site in the file at once — no
per-function change needed.

The 30-second constant matches the default timeout used by sibling channel plugins (e.g.
Feishu registration paths, `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.ts:25`).

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled or slow `chat.googleapis.com` endpoint (or a network device between
the gateway and Google) leaves the outbound reply call pending indefinitely. No timeout
error is surfaced; gateway lanes accumulate.

**After:** Every outbound Google Chat API request fails with an abort/timeout error after
30 seconds. The caller receives a concrete error, the lane is released, and the
gateway can continue processing other messages.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/googlechat-api-request-timeout`  
Base: `upstream/main` (`c69724ef3b508eb42189d1731c1bcd85027ddb22`)  
Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/api.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ Google Chat API request timeout > passes timeoutMs to fetchWithSsrFGuard on every outbound request 39ms
 ✓ Google Chat API request timeout > aborts with a timeout error when the API stalls 1ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  329ms
```

Test 1 asserts `fetchWithSsrFGuard` receives a positive numeric `timeoutMs` on a real
`sendGoogleChatMessage` call.  
Test 2 asserts that when `fetchWithSsrFGuard` rejects with an `AbortError` (the error
shape produced by an expired timeout), the caller receives a rejected promise rather than
hanging.

### Source-level proof

```json
{"constant_defined":true,"passed_to_fetchWithSsrFGuard":true,"timeout_value_ms":30000}
```

`GOOGLECHAT_API_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` is defined and wired as `timeoutMs` inside
`withGoogleChatResponse`, so all call paths through the shared helper carry the deadline.

### Format and lint

```
$ git diff --check   →  (no output, clean)
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs … extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts extensions/googlechat/src/api.test.ts
oxlint OK
```

### Diff summary

```
extensions/googlechat/src/api.ts      |  5 +++++ (constant + timeoutMs field)
extensions/googlechat/src/api.test.ts | 65 +++++  (new file — 2 regression cases)
```

### Reproduction sketch (end-to-end)

1. Stand up a TCP server that accepts connections on port 443 and sends a valid TLS
   handshake but never emits an HTTP response (e.g. `openssl s_server` / custom Node
   server returning nothing after accept).
2. Route `chat.googleapis.com` to that server in `/etc/hosts`.
3. Trigger a Google Chat inbound message that produces an agent reply.
4. **Before fix:** `withGoogleChatResponse` never resolves — gateway lane stays open
   indefinitely.
5. **After fix:** Call aborts after 30 s with `AbortError: The operation timed out`,
   error is logged, lane is released.

What was not tested: a live `chat.googleapis.com` stall scenario with a real Google
Workspace account. Crabbox/Testbox remote CI was not available at submission time.
